The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondents for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.

2. The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 06.12.2022 at about 8.45 p.m. Guruprashanth was driving his autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-02-AG- 1777 ON Kodavatti Junction Bypass Road, Huliyurdurga Town, Kunial Taluk, Tumkur, at that time, all of a sudden Tipper Lorry Goods Carrying bearing Reg.No.KA- 16-C-4403 driven by its driver at high speed in rash and negligent manner and came on wrong lane and dashed against the autorickshaw,
due to the said impact, Guruprashanth fell down on left side of the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the SCCH 5 accident, he was shifted to Adichunchanagiri Institute of Medical Science Hospital, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient, but inspite of best treatment given by the Doctors, he succumbed to the injuries during the course of treatment on 08.12.2022.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Petitioners have spent a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical, hospitalization, food and nourishment,
funeral and obsequies ceremony.

At the time of accident, deceased was aged about 39 years, working as Auto Driver, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.

petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are minor daughters,
petitioner No.4 is mother of the deceased Guruprashanth, due to sudden demise of the deceased,
petitioners have suffered irreparable loss, damage, untold misery.

Out of the said accident, crime No.196/2022 is registered against the driver of the Tipper Lorry Goods bearing Reg.No.
KA-16-C-4403 before the Huliyurdurga Police for the offences punishable under SCCH 5 Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
R1 is the R.C.Owner, R2 is the insurer of the said tipper lorry, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
So that, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/-.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has R1/owner has appeared and filed written statement and denied entire averments of the petition.

Further denied age, occupation, income,
occurrence of the accident.
Further submitted that, he is owner of the tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16-C-4403 and the said vehicle is insured with respondent No.2.
claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.

Further stated that, petition is bad for non- SCCH 5 joinder of necessary and proper parties and driver of the autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-02-AG-1777 was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Further denied that alleged accident was occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of the tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16-C-4403.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
He is entitled to take shelter under Sec.147 and 149 of M.V.Act.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:

::ISSUES::
1.
Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Sri.Guruprashanth, S/o.

Late. Puttappa @ Puttaiah Urf Hombaiah, succumbed to the death by injuries sustained in vehicular SCCH 5 accident alleged to have been occurred on 06.12.2022 at about 8.45 p.m. due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the Tipper Lorry,
bearing Reg.No.KA-16-C-4403?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3.
What order or award?

On the other hand, respondents have not adduced any evidence.
8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.

Then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:

9. Issue No.1:- In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1/wife of the deceased has deposed her evidence as PW-1, in her chief-examination she has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of inquest is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of spot mahazar with sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of vehicle seizure mahazar is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of P.M. 10.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and the records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint, inquest,
spot mahazar with sketch, vehicle seizure mahazar, SCCH 5 P.M.Report, 133 notice, reply notice IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioners about causing of the accident dated 06.12.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.

Per contra, except appearance and filing written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non- causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioners about death of Guruprashanth out of the accident held on 06.12.2022 at about 8.45 p.m. while he was driving autorickshaw bearing Reg.No. KA-02-AG- 1777 on Jkodavatti Junction Bypass Road, Huliyurdurga Town, Kunigal Tqaluk, Tumkur.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioners.
SCCH 5 12.

On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the Tipper Lorry Goods carrying bearing Reg.No.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioners, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioners have proved the above issue No.1 in their favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-

As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/Guru Prashanth was aged about 39 years as on the date of accident, for proof of age of the deceased, petitioners have furnished copy of driving license marked as Ex.P.12, wherein date of birth is mentioned as 21.09.1983, the alleged accident was occurred on 06.12.2022.

Accordingly relying on driving license of the deceased, age of the deceased is considered about SCCH 5 40 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 15 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,750/- p.m.

To prove the said facts, they have furnished notarized copy of aadhar cards of SCCH 5 petitioner No.1 to 4 are marked as Ex.P.11 it reveals that, they are legal representatives of the deceased Guruprashanth, hence they will become dependents of the deceased.

16. As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the number of dependents are 4 to 6, then 1/4th of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/4th of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

17. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, The Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 40% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged upto 40 years, in case of self employed person or person having fixed salary as future prospects.

Further petitioner No.1 being the wife of the deceased is entitled for Rs.20,000/- towards consortium.

Petitioner No.2 and 3 being minor children of the SCCH 5 deceased are entitled for Rs.20,000/- each towards loss of parental consortium and petitioner No.4 being mother of the deceased is entitled for Rs.20,000/- towards filial consortium.
Further they are entitled for loss of estate of Rs.15,000/- and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/-.

with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
22.

In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Tipper Goods Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16-C-4403 bearing No.2315 2041 0217 4001 001 which is valid from 22.06.2022 to 21.06.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 06.12.2022 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.
Hence naturally liability of R1 shall go against R2, so that, R2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.28,97,660/- (Rupees Twenty Eight Lakhs Ninety Seven Thousand Six Hundred Sixty Only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 60:10:10:20 in the award amount.

The petitioners No.1 and 4 are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be SCCH 5 kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
Since Petitioner No.2 and 3 are minors, on deposit of the award amount, entire share shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank till he attains age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in the name of minor Petitioner guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor Petitioners.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
